title: If the account was joint
description: The person who died shared a bank account with someone, or was the only holder.
opening: A joint account is shared by two or more people. What happens after a death depends on how the account was opened.

official.text: For joint accounts opened as "either or survivor" or "anyone or survivor", the bank can pay the surviving holder.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 7(a) and 8: "either or survivor" and "anyone or survivor" accounts; payment to the survivor(s) is a valid discharge.

official.text: The survivor receives the money as a trustee of the legal heirs, which means they hold it for the heirs.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 8(iii): "as a trustee of the legal heirs of the deceased depositor(s)".

official.text: In a joint account, the nominee's right starts only after all the account holders have died.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 8: "the nominee's right arises only after the death of all the depositors".

official.text: To close a joint fixed deposit early, the bank needs the consent of the surviving holders and of the legal heirs of the person who died.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 14: premature termination "shall require the consent of the surviving depositors and the legal heir(s) of the deceased joint holder".

official.text: If the person was the only holder and named a nominee, the bank should not insist on a succession certificate, whatever the amount.
official.confirms: RBI Directions 2025, para 9: "the bank shall not insist on production of legal documents such as Succession Certificate", "irrespective of the amount".

suggestions: Look at the passbook or the account opening form for words like "either or survivor". Ask the bank if you are not sure.
Tell the bank about the death before anyone uses the account.
If the account had only one holder and no nominee, read the page "If there is no nominee".
lawyer: The surviving holder and the legal heirs do not agree about the money.
The way the account was opened is unclear, and the bank asks for court papers.
A child under 18 is a holder or an heir.
sourceNeeded: Who the bank pays when a joint account has no survivor clause. The RBI directions we read do not say it directly.
